facts.subject: Cross-run deduplication is not supplied by these guards
facts.finding: Attempt1 applies separately to each workflow run. A different run can also be attempt1. The ref-based concurrency group serializes eligible runs; it does not act as a durable consumed-operation record. Run-ID-specific directories/controllers give a distinct run a distinct local namespace. The inspected source contains no expected-before/after pair guard, durable cross-run claim of this old/new pair, or prior-run deduplication lookup.
facts.inference_limit: These source facts do not prove that a second run would actually be created by an identical API update. They show only that the workflow/helper cannot independently certify at-most-once execution across separately created eligible runs.

facts.subject: Documented update guard versus atomic at-most-once claim
facts.finding: The exposed update_ref declaration says a mismatched expected_sha is rejected. It does not specify implementation linearizability, a durable idempotency key, cancellation, or recovery of a prior request's result. GitHub's public Update a reference REST contract lists sha and force in the body; it does not document an expected-old body parameter. The underlying wrapper implementation was not available and was not inferred.
facts.conditional_reasoning: A genuinely atomic compare-and-swap from old to new, combined with no intervening reset/recreation to old, permits at most one successful old-to-new transition among competing calls. An at-most-one hosted execution claim additionally requires a proved relationship between that single transition and delivery/creation of workflow runs. Neither the necessary end-to-end guarantees nor complete ref history are established here.
facts.inference_limit: No claim that the wrapper is non-atomic, that a reset occurred, or that a duplicate run exists. No claim that a future successful update would retroactively prove the first call was untransmitted.
